candidates.name: Exact mixed difference over hybrids plus common-hybrid witness cover (singleton cancellation under vertex deletion)
paper_items: lem q:mixed-difference 'Exact centering before absolute values' (quantitative/04-paths-trace.tex:351-375)
lem q:witness-cover 'A common configuration of witnesses' (quantitative/05-rank-witness.tex:236-286)
candidates.trace: PV9 (L164-171, summarizer: 'combinatorial turning point'); trace E1
candidates.statement: For a closed word with singleton prime set U, the deletion-damaged centred word expectation is at most 1_lit-consistent * b_L * E[R |Delta G|], where Delta G = sum_{H subset U} (-1)^{|U|-|H|} G_H runs over 'hybrid' residue configurations (singletons in H overwritten by their forced residues). If |U| > L^{1/4} and Delta G != 0, expanding G = prod_w (1 - I_w) shows that some single hybrid contains positive witnesses whose prime supports cover U. A minimal cover yields T = L^{1/12} witnesses with private singleton primes. Active labels then give T successively eliminable congruences, each saving (1+L)/H_0.

neighbours.ref: Pilatte 2026 (arXiv:2310.19357v3), Prop. 9.1 with Lemma 9.2 and Lemma 9.4(1),(3)
neighbours.relation: Same principle: after a truncated combinatorial sieve expands the deletion indicator, only terms whose modulus contains all singleton primes escape cancellation (Lemma 9.2: d_S does not divide q_R implies near-perfect cancellation). The rank bound (9.4(1)) then excludes small-rank terms. 007 replaces the truncated sieve and its coefficient and remainder bounds with an exact mixed difference that is used only to show existence, and replaces the rank with a minimal cover and private primes.

neighbours.ref: Helfgott-Radziwill 2021, section 5, Prop. 5.1 'Obtaining cancellation from lone primes'
neighbours.relation: Poses exactly the obstruction 007's lemma solves: restrict A to the sieved set and still get cancellation among walks with many lone primes. Solved by the combinatorial sieve plus the Kubilius model.
neighbours.verdict: close variant (same problem and role, different machinery)

neighbours.relation: The mixed difference over U annihilates every summand that does not depend on all coordinates in U. This is exactly the step 'a subfamily whose supports omit p has zero mixed difference'.

candidates.name: Two-band weighted divisor graph: uncentred heavily weighted core primes plus vertex-normalised centre primes with non-mean-zero centring theta = beta_Z^2
paper_items: lem:trace-integration good-edge computation (qualitative/trace-count.tex:336-373) and modified subtree weights eq:modified-subtree-sum (trace-count.tex:100-115)
candidates.trace: PV4 (L94-99, L117-121); insight backtrack I.a4.5 -> I.a4.6 (medium confidence); trace E2
candidates.statement: Edge kernel g_d(x,y) = w_d(x)w_d(y) A^{omega_C(d)} 1_{d_C | x} prod_{p|d, p in Z}(1_{p|x} - theta/p). The core band C (weight A = e^{2 kappa}, uncentred) supplies size and cutoff savings; the centre band Z (weight 1) supplies cancellation. With vertex weight W(x) = prod_a beta_a^{-omega_a(x)} and closed-walk products normalised by W at each departure, a centre prime on a single good edge has total multiplier theta(1-theta/p) on its lit residue and -theta beta_Z^{nu_p(a)}/p elsewhere. The choice theta = beta_Z^2 cancels the O(1/p) terms before absolute values, leaving O(theta(l+1)/p^2).

candidates.name: Finite residue comparison via Braverman's bounded independence, with the Alon-Goldreich-Mansour exact-independence correction
paper_items: cor q:finite-expansion, cor q:truncated-weight, active Q-state expansion (02-finite-law.tex:156-235)
applied in Thm q:trace (04-paths-trace.tex, eq q:word-comparison-budget) and lem q:bad
candidates.trace: PV8 (L159-163, conflict C18: the CRT modulus exceeds the interval); trace E3. The AGM step is not visible in the trace.
candidates.statement: Every event given by a depth-at-most-20, size-at-most-exp(L^6) circuit in residue-equality tests modulo primes up to e^L has the same probability, up to e^{-L^{10}}, under a uniform origin in any interval of length at least exp(L^A/2) as under the independent product law. Proof: encode residues by B = L^15 jittered dyadic bits; bound t-wise bit marginals by CRT; correct to exact t-wise uniformity by a Fourier/AGM step; apply Braverman (Corollary 2).

provenance_flag.explanation: The cited 2025-2026 works are Pilatte (v1 2023, human), TT26 (v1 Dec 2025) and the KMT 2026 version. None discloses AI help for anything a candidate depends on. TT26 discloses ChatGPT for figure code ('the text in this paper is entirely human-generated') and credits a GPT 5.4 Thinking forum observation on an unrelated irrationality problem. These are summarizer-relayed quotes, so they are unverified. That disclosure does not touch the correlation estimate, and no 007 candidate has a counterpart in TT26. Web and catalog searches found no model-produced prior work on ordinary two-point Chowla or binary Elliott. One caveat: Pilatte's JAMS version (2026-09-10) is the template for the whole method and appeared 14 days before the paper date. That is a human precedent and a timing note, not model provenance.

bridge_novelty.import: TCS pseudorandomness -> analytic number theory: Braverman's 'polylog-wise independence fools AC0', plus the AGM almost-to-exact correction, used to compare integer interval averages with the independent residue law (C3)
bridge_novelty.classification: new bridge for a known role
bridge_novelty.evidence: No prior application of Braverman, Bazzi or Tal-type AC0 fooling to sieve or correlation problems was found (two WebSearch queries). Green 2012 links Mobius and AC0 only in the opposite direction, via LMN. The role (integer vs independent-model comparison) is filled in HR21 section 3.3 by a multidimensional Kubilius model. Linial-Nisan's approximate inclusion-exclusion is a known conceptual link between Bonferroni/Brun truncation and bounded independence, so the route was signposted.

Exclude the OpenAI internal model that produced 007 and its ChatGPT Pro lineage from the main pool; run them only as an uncontrolled reference arm. The judge must not be the proposer. An analytic number theorist checks all hits and 10% of misses. Lean equivalence where available (e.g. TwoPoint/Bounds/MixedDifference.lean; OrdinaryCorrelations/HighTrace/BetaZ.lean). Hits that reproduce the Pilatte-precedent route are scored in a separate 'precedent reproduction' column.

P-C1.item: C1 mixed difference plus common-hybrid witness cover
P-C1.hide: q:mixed-difference, q:witness-cover, q:active-definition, q:active, q:singletons, and everything downstream: 06-forest completion, q:trace-completion, 07-spectral final steps, 08-affine
P-C1.give: 01-03 (setup, finite law, analytic), 04-paths-trace up to eq q:word-product including lit/unlit expansion and q:many-unlit, q:rank-probability and q:rank
P-C1.obstacle_statement: Without vertex deletion, a singleton centred factor integrates to zero. With the deletion G, show that words with more than L^{1/4} singleton primes contribute exp(-L^{1+c}).
P-C1.equivalence: Hit if the proposal (a) bounds the damaged centred expectation by an exact discrete-derivative or mixed-difference quantity over the singleton coordinates, or an equivalent sieve-free exact identity, and (b) deduces that a nonzero term forces witnesses, simultaneously positive in one configuration, whose supports cover (or many of which privately contain) the singleton primes, giving many eliminable congruences. Pilatte-style truncated sieve plus Lemma 9.2 plus rank is scored as 'precedent reproduction', not as a hit.

P-C2.item: C2 two-band theta-centred weighted divisor graph
P-C2.hide: graph-setup (eq:prime-bands, eq:graph-kernel, eq:graph-weights, prop:graph-estimate) and everything downstream: analytic-transfer, paths, thinning, cylinder-sieve, trace-count, localization
P-C2.give: Introduction minus 'Main ideas' paragraphs 3-4; MRT Thm 1.7; the order-of-limits device C4; Pilatte and HR21

arms_specific.A_with_part_I: also give Part I (quantitative), whose padding plus centred-supply architecture is the internal sibling

P-C2.obstacle_statement: Adapt the Helfgott-Radziwill/Pilatte graph method to ordinary averages of general bounded multiplicative functions under a rate-free non-pretentiousness hypothesis. A fixed-scale graph must beat a B^{-1} bias by a power of B.
P-C2.equivalence: Hit if the proposal (i) splits primes into an uncentred, heavily weighted class used for size and cutoff savings and a centred class used for cancellation, and (ii) when the centred class enters the vertex normalisation, chooses its centring constant as the tilted mean (theta = beta^2 for unit weight, or the general beta_a^2-type formula), so that one-edge primes cancel in closed-walk products. (i) without (ii), or (ii) without (i), is partial credit.

P-C3.obstacle_statement: The prime supplies grow with X, so their joint CRT modulus exceeds the interval length. Compare integer-interval averages of bounded-depth residue tests with the independent product law to error e^{-L^{10}}.
P-C3.equivalence: Hit if the proposal invokes bounded independence fooling AC0 (Braverman, Bazzi, Tal), with any exact-independence correction. Kubilius-model or fundamental-lemma solutions are recorded separately as 'alternative route' and checked for validity.
